1Google ships Gemini 4 Argon to everyone

@GoogleDeepMind — Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available · 13 Oct 17:05 WAT. Below: @cursor_ai on CursorBench and price.

Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Argon worldwide on 13 Oct. It is in the Gemini API, in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra users, and in Antigravity for Ultra users. Logan Kilpatrick says over 100,000 Google staff tested it for a month, and it can give up to 1M tokens of output. Cursor says it scores 52.8% on CursorBench at default effort, on par with Opus 5.5, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

Why it matters: Google now has a frontier model at a low price. But first reviews are mixed: Ben’s Bites found it slow and weak at design. Test it on your own tasks before you switch.

Source quote

Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available.

2Anthropic replaces git: 30,000 merges a day

@AnthropicAI — Creating in-house source control · 13 Oct 17:36 WAT.

Anthropic says it merged about 2,500 code changes per day in May and more than 30,000 per day in September. Tools built for human speed became a bottleneck. In five months, a small team built a new version control system and moved the full monorepo off git. Zvi Mowshowitz reports that the internal system is called Scion.

Why it matters: This is a clear sign of how much code agents now write. Normal developer tools may not hold at agent scale.

Source quote

In May, we merged around 2,500 code changes per day. In September, we merged more than 30,000 per day.

@AnthropicAI · 13 Oct 2026 · 7.9M views
@AnthropicAI · 13 Oct 2026 17:36 WATPost

3Anthropic’s leaked Q3: $16.8bn revenue, and still a “miss”

Exponential View — Anthropic: The agony and the ecstasy · 15 Oct. Below: @simonw on distillation revenue.

Azeem Azhar summarizes a leaked Anthropic investor briefing. Reported Q3 revenue is $16.8bn, almost 4x all of 2025. Reported adjusted gross margin is 85%. Azhar still calls it a miss, because a July leak had set a $65bn annualized target. He writes that Korea’s KOSPI fell 7.57% that day. Simon Willison quotes a report that distillation by other labs was 5–7% of Anthropic’s revenue.

Why it matters: These are leaked numbers, not audited results. They show that AI revenue grows very fast, but market expectations grow faster.

Source quote

And yet it’s a miss.

4OpenAI and Anthropic each give $5M for AI in mathematics

@OpenAI · 15 Oct 15:35 WAT. Below: @AnthropicAI · 15 Oct 22:31 WAT.

On the same day, OpenAI and Anthropic each committed $5 million to the Simons Foundation. The money pays for workshops, conferences and programs that help mathematicians check and build on results from AI. Both labs also give model access and compute.

Why it matters: AI now produces math results that people must verify. The labs pay the math community to do that work.

Source quote

we are contributing $5 million to a new Simons Foundation initiative to help mathematicians examine, understand, and build on results produced by AI

5Grok Voice 3.0 leads voice; Grok Bot grows fast

@elonmusk · 14 Oct 22:32 WAT. Below: 15 Oct 23:52 WAT.

Elon Musk says Grok Voice 3.0 is now the leading conversational voice model. Ben’s Bites reports that it tops the speech-to-speech rankings and handles about 20,000 Starlink support calls a day. Musk also says Grok Bot grows faster than anything he has seen, and that it has no free tier.

Why it matters: Voice agents now do real support work at scale. The growth claim is the founder’s own; no user numbers were given.

Medium

Sandboxes: do you know what your agents are doing?

The author builds an agent harness in a regulated company. He reviews the 2026 agent incidents and says a system prompt tells an agent what it should do, but does not enforce what it can do. A sandbox closes that gap.

Why it matters: Before an agent touches real systems, someone must know it exists, own it, scope it and be able to stop it.

Source quote

The system prompt tells the agent what it should do. It doesn’t enforce what the agent can do.

Jordan Carson · AI Advances · 14 Oct 2026 12:31 WATArticle
Medium

Not every agent mistake costs the same

An extra follow-up question and a confident wrong answer are both errors, but the cost is different. Teams must agree which mistakes are acceptable and which must stop the agent. A higher score can hide worse failures.

Why it matters: Use this before you give an agent more responsibility: score errors by their consequences.

Source quote

A higher score can hide worse failures

Zvi AI #190: Scion, Argon, Wonder

Zvi Mowshowitz · Don’t Worry About the Vase · 15 Oct 2026 13:03 WAT

Weekly roundup. Google’s Argon came with a robust safety report. Meta’s Muse Wonder benchmarks looked “rather sus” to him. OpenAI caught an employee planting a bug. A group used ChatGPT to build a full-chain Chrome exploit and claimed a $250,000 bounty.

Why it matters: Both new frontier models still need independent tests. Security risks now come from inside and outside the labs.
